sentences.text: Lycorhinus was a small herbivorous dinosaur measuring about 1.2 meters in length that possessed long canines in its jaws.

Sidney H. Haughton described the genus Lycorhinus in 1924 based on a partial jaw found in the Upper Elliot Formation of South Africa. The name combines Ancient Greek words for "wolf" and "nose." Originally, the material was thought to be a cynodont, but it has since degraded to a single tooth and an impression of the jaw.

Barrett suggested in 2000 that Lycorhinus was likely omnivorous based on its teeth and canine. Butler and colleagues suggested in 2008 that Lycorhinus used its canines for defense and occasional omnivory. Porro and colleagues suggested in 2010 that Lycorhinus ate tough, fibrous vegetation. Norman et al. suggested in 2011 that Lycorhinus did not use its canines for display or cropping vegetation.

Crompton and Charig identified Lycorhinus as an ornithischian in 1962, while Romer classified it within the ornithopod family Hypsilophodontidae. Later, Sereno identified it as the earliest-diverging member of the Gondwanan clade Heterodontosaurinae.

Lycorhinus lived during the Early Jurassic, specifically the Sinemurian stage. Uranium-lead dating in 2020 confirmed the Upper Elliot Formation spans from approximately 201.3 mya to at least 191.9 mya. This formation spans from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian stages, approximately 201.3 to 190.8 million years ago. The animal lived during the early Jurassic, approximately 203 to 197 million years ago, in what is now Africa.

Charig and Crompton considered Lycorhinus a nomen dubium due to insufficient material to determine if it was the same genus as Heterodontosaurus. Conversely, Hopson argued that Lycorhinus is a valid diagnostic genus distinct from Heterodontosaurus and Abrictosaurus. Lycorhinus consors was considered a nomen dubium because its description was inadequate. In 1978, Thulborn maintained that Heterodontosaurus tucki and Abrictosaurus consors were species of Lycorhinus but proposed that Lanasaurus might not be a heterodontosaurid.
